title: Tabbouleh
subtitle: Lebanese parsley and bulgur salad
excerpt: A bright, fresh salad built on very finely chopped flat-leaf parsley with bulgur wheat, tomato, spring onion, and lemon. The parsley is the main ingredient, not the bulgur.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tabbouleh is one of the most recognisable dishes of Lebanese cooking and is widely made across the Levant. The Lebanese version is primarily parsley, with a very small amount of bulgur wheat, which distinguishes it from western versions where the ratio is sometimes reversed.

content.text: Tabbouleh is a herb salad, not a grain salad. The main ingredient is a very large quantity of flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped to almost a paste, with a small amount of bulgur wheat, ripe tomato, spring onion, mint, lemon, and olive oil. The knife work is the whole technique, and the dressing is added at the end so the herbs stay sharp and bright.
Cover the bulgur wheat with cold water and leave to soak for 20 minutes. Drain through a fine sieve, pressing out as much water as possible.
Very finely chop the parsley leaves and mint. They should be almost powdery, not chunky. Put in a large bowl with the soaked bulgur.
Salt the diced tomato and leave it in a sieve for 5 minutes to drain off excess liquid. Add to the bowl with the spring onions.
Add the lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss together gently. Taste and adjust with more lemon or salt. The salad should be sharp, herby, and bright. Serve immediately or within an hour.
